title: The search help now says "add - to exclude".
TriOS can read each mod's site details from a new file
body: mod-catalog-extras.json is published beside the catalog with each mod's releases, gallery, requirements, save answers, AI use and Discord post. The viewer's home page shows how many mods it holds.

title: Readers can report a problem with a mod or the site
body: Each mod page has a "Report a problem" link under its details, and the footer has one for the site itself. Both open a GitHub issue form with the mod, page and site version filled in.

title: Forum pictures with "&" in their address load again
body: Pictures hosted on Dropbox and similar sites now show on mod cards and in galleries, including on topics already saved. Pictures the model could not read for this reason will be looked at again.

title: Mods from a shared thread list each other
body: A mod read off a thread or Discord post holding other mods now says "From the forum thread <name>." or "From the Discord post <name>." under its name. Pressing the name opens a box listing every mod from that thread, with a button to the thread itself.

title: Hovering an author's name shows the other names they go by.
Shortened release links now appear before debug builds in mod downloads.
Browse says how many mods your filters hide, and icons are sharp
body:
The line above the results now says "N hidden by your filters." with a "Clear filters" link, in place of the line that only counted the AI filter. The search and the game version are not counted.

Icons beside words are no longer moved by part of a pixel, which made them fuzzy. The Cards and Rows icons are redrawn so their lines sit on whole pixels.

title: The date filters are sliders
body: Posted and Last edited are now sliders with two ends you can drag, and a calendar button at each end picks an exact day. The date filters have no hover text.

title: About links to the forum and the Discord
Browse and Home can filter by date
body: Two date filters, Posted and Last edited, each take a first and a last day. Last edited is the latest day the author edited the forum post, their follow-up posts or the Discord messages. Saved filters and shared links keep the dates.

title: A tooltip no longer stays on screen after you go to another page.
Reports no longer has a line under its heading
Starmodder no longer links to or names Nexus Mods
body: Mod pages, the fallback button, the picture viewer and the picture setting no longer mention Nexus Mods. The About page still does.

title: The download button beside the globe button has room for its words
body:
"Install with TriOS" and its logo were squeezed into three quarters of a
148-pixel column. The globe button is now a fixed 34 pixels, the download
takes the rest, and the column is 168 pixels.

title: Dividers and link underlines in posts are thin lines, as on the forum
body:
A divider is now one faint 1px line instead of the browser's two-pixel
ridge. A link's underline is 1px at every text size, so a big link in a
post's title is no longer underlined heavily.

title: The default dark theme is a lighter grey, and Independents comes in two shades
body:
On dark screens, Browser Default keeps Independents' grey and yellow on a
lighter grey background. The text is a little darker to match, so it reads
the same against the panels. Settings lists this as "Independents", and the
darker look it had before as "Independents (Darker)". Readers who picked
Independents before keep the darker look.

title: Code blocks in forum posts sit in a box, and dividers have more room
body:
A code block now has its own background, border and padding, as on the
forum. Long lines scroll sideways instead of wrapping, and a long block
scrolls inside its box. Dividers have a little under a line of room above
and below them, as on the forum.

title: Forum posts keep their heading sizes and left-aligned lists
body:
Text sizes in a forum post are now judged against the forum's 10pt body
text instead of 12pt. A 12pt section heading was shown at body size; it is
now one step bigger, as on the forum. A list inside a centred block now
stays left-aligned, so each line starts beside its bullet.

title: Download buttons show the TriOS, Discord and forum icons
body: "Install with TriOS" buttons show the TriOS triangle. Cards and rows draw it with one dot in the middle, and a mod's page draws the logo's nine dots. A mod with nothing to download now shows the Discord, forum or Nexus Mods icon on its "On Discord" style button on cards and rows too. The Discord icon sits a little lower, so it lines up with the words.

title: Home's Filters bar takes less room when shut.
Changelog answers are shorter
body: Changelog notes come from the author's post, found by each entry's version and first and last few words. An entry that can't be found in the post is dropped. Downloads use their number in the post's list of links. Answers on posts with long changelogs are about 70% shorter, and every topic is read again on the next coverage pass.

title: Browse and Home can filter by where a mod was posted.
body:
The new From filter keeps mods on the forum's mod index, mods with any forum
thread, or mods posted on Discord. Browse has a "Copy filters from Home"
button that works like Home's copy button. Home's filter bar now sits under
the AI summaries banner. The side column's panels are in a new order, and
Show is now called Filter.

title: Settings has an Accessibility section.
body: Animations offers Default, On and Off. Default follows the device's reduce motion setting. Off stops animations and keeps GIFs on their first frame until opened in the picture viewer. Settings groups have a line between them.

title: Forum spoilers in the newer format show as folds again.
body:
The forum now writes a spoiler as <details class="bbc_spoiler">. The site
dropped those tags, so a spoiler's title ran into its text ("LicenseThis
mod is..."). 41 saved posts use this format.

title: The takedown box links to Wispborne's forum profile.
Filters on Home, and saved filters
body: Home has its own filter bar at the top: game version, category, requirements, the switches and AI use. It starts with every filter off, and a button copies the filters from the Browse page after asking to confirm. Filters can be saved under a name and reused on Home and Browse. Browse now keeps its remembered filters when opened from a link. The AI preset "No vibecode" is now "No vibecoded mods".

title: A taken-down mod's page shows Not found straight away
body: A taken-down mod's old address now shows the not-found page from the next publish. Before, Cloudflare could keep showing the old page for up to a week.

title: The changelog page warns that its entries are AI-written.
The TriOS link on About opens TriOS's page on Starmodder.
Mod authors can see how to ask for a mod to be removed
body: Every mod page and the About page have a "Remove mod from Starmodder" button. It says how to message Wisp from the account that posts the mod.

title: AI use filter presets
body: The AI use filter on Browse now opens with presets: No filter, No AI, Absolutely no AI, No AI images, No vibecode and Custom. The part, mode and level controls show only under Custom, and a preset is one key in the address.

title: How to install mods guide
body: A "How to install mods" guide now has its own page, and the button for it in the top bar opens it in a box over the current page. The box can hide the button from the bar, and the guide is always on the About page. About moved to the right end of the bar beside Settings, and every entry in the bar lines up on one line.

title: Mod pages list optional mods
body: A mod page now shows the mods its post calls optional or recommended as outlined chips under Requires. Every post and Discord thread is read again by the LLM to find them.

title: Requirements written differently now point at the same mod
body: "Lazy Lib", "GraphicLib" and "IndEvo" now lead to LazyLib, GraphicsLib and Industrial Evolution, and the Browse filter lists each mod once. Names the rules cannot match are sent to the LLM, and the viewer has a Dependencies page for fixing matches by hand.

title: The not-found page's first link now reads Go Home.
Mods can be taken down
body: A mod, or every mod credited to one person, can now be taken off the catalog, the mod details, Starmodder and ModRepo.json from the viewer's new Takedowns page or a "Take down" button. The confirm box shows exactly which mods go and which spellings matched. Restoring brings a mod back at its old address. The takedown list is published with the outputs, and a publish stops if it has lost an entry. Missing addresses on Starmodder now show a not-found page.

title: Changelog page
body: Starmodder has a Changelog page, linked from the footer next to Release feed and from the About page. It lists every change to the site, newest first, and is written from the git history each time the site is built. The About page's buttons now sit at the top, each with an icon.

title: Reports page
body: Starmodder has a Reports page after Favorites: dependency use count, mods by game version, new mods by month, mods by category and updates by week. Each bar opens Browse with the matching filter. Game versions with a typo, such as "0.9.8a" or "0.81a", are now grouped under the real release on Browse and Reports, and a version of "-" counts as no version. Spellings of one required mod, such as "Lazy Lib" and "LazyLib", count as one in the Requires filter.

title: Linked pictures in forum posts open in the picture viewer
body:
A picture in a forum post that links to itself or to a picture host now opens
in the viewer instead of a new tab. The viewer says where each picture came
from: "Image from forum", "Image from Discord" or "Image from Nexus Mods",
linked to that page.

title: Browser Default uses Independents on dark pages
body: The old cyan-on-navy theme is now called TriOS. Its id stays "dark", so readers who picked it keep it.

title: The AI use tooltip heads the author's quote "AI Disclosure".
Spoiler tags left as text become folds
body:
The forum leaves every [spoiler] tag in a post as plain text when the
tags don't pair up (topic 35818). The site now pairs them itself. A tag
that is never closed, or a pair that would cut through other HTML tags,
stays as text.

title: A mod with no AI use statement shows "Unknown", with "No AI use declaration found." on hover.
Viewer shows each picture in a thread's image list
body: Picture ratings now read "good for a mod card" on Starmodder and in the viewer.

title: Show everything the AI saw in each picture
body: The viewer's thread page lists each picture's kind, card fit, description or error, model, endpoint, time and caption prompt version. On Starmodder, gallery hover text and the picture viewer add the picture's kind and card fit, or say the AI could not open it.

title: Starmodder shows what each mod's author says about AI use
body: The model reads what a post says about AI tools, and each mod page has an "AI use" line under Details with the author's words on hover. Browse has an AI use filter: "Don't show AI-gen…" or "Only show AI-gen…" for the kinds of content checked, how much AI work counts, and whether optional AI content counts. Search has has:ai and is:noai. The side filter panels remember whether they are open. The model also skips lists of an author's other mods and treats stripped-down builds as variants.

title: Gallery pictures show the AI's description of them
body: On Starmodder, a gallery picture's hover text and the caption in the picture viewer can be the AI's description, marked "AI description:". It follows the reader's AI summary setting and the "Hide AI summaries" switch on mod pages.

title: The model can look at each post's pictures before reading it
body: With the picture setting on, the model describes each picture once and sees those descriptions when it reads the post. The viewer shows them under each picture. Starmodder now picks a mod's card picture from those ratings, and mod artwork kept in an icons folder is no longer dropped.

title: The scraper reads the forum again after its move to SMF 2.1
body: The mod index, board listings and each thread's author rank and last edit date are read from SMF 2.1 pages again. Starmodder keeps the new forum's centring, quotes, code blocks and typewriter text in mod descriptions.

title: A list of mods linking to their own threads no longer gives each one a second page
body: A mod on a forum post that only links to its own forum thread now appears once, from that thread. Its old address from the list leads to the mod on that thread.

title: Old mod addresses lead to the mod they were joined into
body: When two pages for one mod become one, the old address now opens the joined mod's page instead of nothing, keeping any tab picked after it. The catalog comparison lists these separately from the missing ones.

title: Shorter LLM prompt and plainer viewer wording
body: The LLM's instructions are shorter, and every forum topic and Discord thread is read again once. Starmodder's Settings and the AI summary banner now offer the same three choices, with "Only if missing" renamed to "Only as a fallback".

title: Fixed Orbiting Spoons getting a new mod id.
The new output files are mod-catalog.json and mod-catalog-details.json
body: The viewer calls them Mod Catalog and Mod Details, with Catalog explorer, Catalog diff and Details diff under Debug. The Home banner and file cards have plainer wording.

title: Old forum threads no longer show up as recently added
body:
The mod index still lists old threads whose posts were never saved, such
as theDragn's 0.95a threads. With no post there is no date, so the site
used the day the mod got its id, which put them at the top of Recently
added. A mod whose forum thread was never read now gets no added date.

Also gives the Hide button on the AI summaries banner a cyan border, and
notes in CLAUDE.md that the public site is called Starmodder.

title: The catalog keeps old mod addresses through more joins
body: The same mod on the forum and Discord now becomes one mod when both offer the same file or the LLM gives both the same name, and one post offering a single file is one mod, not a Collection. An old address stays with the mod that still goes by its name, and a forum topic keeps its own address when its Discord thread moves to another topic. Mod index topics behind the forum login are listed from their index line, and threads with no saved post are left out. Titles become names without stray version bits, "[.98a]" counts as a game version, and the Merge view names the new match. The launch list gains a second viewer on port 8087.

title: One catalog of mods, built from each source post's listings
body:
Every forum topic, Discord thread and Nexus page is read into its
listings first, then one merge builds the catalog. Permanent ids are
found by source post rather than by name. The catalog is written to
ModRepo-v2.json and forum-data-bundle-v2.json; the old two files are
still written the old way until production switches.

The LLM now reads Discord threads too. bin/link_mod_ids.dart links
today's ids to their posts, and bin/compare_catalog.dart compares a
fresh catalog with the published site.

Also on the site: the AI summary choice moves from a cookie to
localStorage, a banner on Home and Browse offers it, and Settings
gets an icon.

title: Browse mods opens with an empty search box
body: Pressing "Browse mods" at the top clears the last search and keeps the other filters. On a mod's page, a download that opens a page is called "Download page" and its hover shows the address, and a download with no file name uses the link's own words. The mod version badge's hover now just says "Mod version". The unified catalog plan is updated too.

title: Search and Browse can ask for mods without something
body:
Typing has:source, has:download, is:addable, is:wip or is:tool in the search keeps the mods that answer yes, and a minus in front leaves them out. from:discord now names where a mod was found, and source: still works.

Browse's switches have a third "not" state, drawn with a red cross, and "Not safe to add mid-game" lists only mods whose author said so. The side column's tick boxes are redrawn, and the search "?" lights up only while its help shows.

title: Search help opens from the "?" even while typing
body: Hovering the "?" opens the search help and hides the suggestions. Clicking back into the search box brings the suggestions back. Both search boxes have a plainer clear button, and DeCell and .7556 are credited as one person.

title: Mod pages no longer flash plain text before they load.
Search engines can read each mod's page and find every mod
body: Each mod's page file now holds the mod's name, authors, summary, links, requirements and the first 500 characters of its forum post. The site also publishes a sitemap.xml listing every mod page, and a robots.txt pointing to it.

title: Mod pages show the Discord post and short related-mod lists
body: A mod's page shows its Discord post under the forum post, and the side column is one panel with "On this page" and short "More by" and "Similar mods" lists that replace the card rows at the foot. TriOS is scraped from its pinned thread, and the mod index reads each mod from today's index only.

title: Card summaries taken from the author's post read as whole sentences
body:
A summary no longer stops at a link or at a line break in the middle of a
sentence, and keeps the author's opening sentences up to about 300 characters.
Summaries cut from inside a centred block or a spoiler no longer start with
"Contents" or "Spoiler" stuck to the first word. The plain-text description
keeps a sentence with a link in it on one line, and lists one item per line.

title: Cards can use the author's own opening sentence as the summary, picked out by the LLM on single-mod threads too.
Spacing is one fixed set of numbers instead of a Dense / Comfortable setting.
Browse rows show everything a card does, and Settings can hide the "Summary generated by AI" text.
Corners are cut at the top left and bottom right, like Starsector's buttons.
Settings show or hide description images with one small switch
body: "Images in descriptions" is now a Show / Hide switch on one line, and the image and AI sections have shorter wording.

title: Settings offer clearer image controls and more theme choices.
body: Browser Default follows the browser, with fixed Dark and Light choices and a One Dark Blue theme. Images in descriptions have one toggle, spacing labels are shorter, and selected view controls have softer highlights.

title: The About page explains moderation, local AI, and its connection to TriOS.
Browse filters default to the side layout.
Browse offers top and side filters and clearer game version choices.
body: Versions follow TriOS ordering. Miscellaneous has its own category name, older game versions stand out on mod pages, and redundant breadcrumbs and search hints are removed.

title: Browse remembers filters and labels linked source code clearly.
Mod pages show source code, license and a cleaner side
body: A mod's page has a Links card with a source code badge (green with the host, or grey "Not linked"), the license by its short name, and support links. The download card sits level with the header and stays pinned, the game version moved from the header to Compatibility, and the side cards are tighter with no divider lines. The gallery shows screenshots only, with small pictures, banners and license badges behind a "Show N small pictures" button.

title: Support links are the author's own, and the mod page is tidied up
body:
The LLM now takes only links that support the mod's own author, each with a short label, so a credits list no longer turns into a row of identical "Support the author" buttons. Forum threads and forms are never support links. Unknown sites are named by their label or host. Draconis Fleet and GraphicsLib are live tests for both sides of this. Every topic is read again on the next LLM pass.

On a mod's page, the open tab is kept in the address, the changelog and release history each have an expand-all button, a "depends" save answer shows a Maybe badge, and the source code sits beside the support links in the download card. Descriptions are published whole, and one that is still cut links to the forum. The footer says the site is not affiliated with Fractal Softworks, and the local site server shows the build from git.

title: A mod's page is two columns, with tabs and a sticky side
body:
The mod sits on the left, under tabs for its description, gallery, changelog and add-ons, and opens with the AI summary, which can be hidden on every mod page. The description is shown whole, with a link to fold it. On the right, one sticky column holds the buttons that get the mod, then compatibility, links, details and every download. A small picture and the one-line summary sit beside the name.

This commit also carries a pass over the site's comments and wording from another session.

title: Search finds mods however their names are typed
body: Punctuation, accents and capitals no longer matter, words can come in any order, and small typos are forgiven, so "seeker unidentified contact" finds Seeker - Unidentified Contact. Shorthand such as "indevo", "kol" and "gl" finds its mod, quotes keep a phrase together, and a minus works on any word. The box at the top now gives the same results as Browse.

title: Mods carry the other names their posts use
body: The LLM now reads each mod's other names off its post, such as "IndEvo" or a name it used to have, and keeps only ones the author really writes. The site publishes them for search and the viewer shows them as "Also called". Every topic is read again on the next LLM pass.

title: Descriptions keep the post's pictures and formatting
body: A mod's description now shows every picture where the author put it, plus the post's text sizes, colours and videos. Pictures can be turned off in Settings or with "Hide pictures" beside the heading, and clicking one opens it full size. The gallery keeps buttons and badges behind a "Show small pictures" button.

title: Read the forum's text sizes, colours and video embeds
body: The builder can now turn a post's sizes, colours and YouTube embeds into the site's own size steps, colours and video ids.

title: The site has a Light theme
body:
Light is the site's own light colours, for a reader who wants light pages
whatever their computer is set to. It repeats the values of the
prefers-color-scheme: light block, because a media query cannot share a
block with a plain selector, so the two have to be changed together.

title: Mod managers and other tools are kept, and marked as tools
body:
The prompt used to call a program run beside the game, like a mod manager,
a non-mod. Since isMod decides whether a thread is kept, a tool with no game
version in its title was dropped from the bundle. Now a tool thread is
isMod: true and each tool entry carries isTool: true, with its downloads
listed like any mod. The flag is on the entry, not the thread, because a
thread can offer a mod and an editor together and because entries reach the
bundle, so TriOS can stop offering to install an .exe as a mod.

- isTool is written only when true, so nothing else in the bundle moves.
- The site publishes it, draws a "Tool" badge and shelves every tool under
  Utilities.
- promptVersion is 20, so every topic is read again.
- A live test pins QBMBAMM (topic 35155) as a tool.

title: Cards show categories and when the mod changed; the favorite star waits for hover
body:
- Cards drop the download count and gain one line of category badges,
  with a "+N" that names the rest at once on hover.
- How long ago a mod changed sits at the bottom right of its picture,
  with an anticlockwise history icon in place of "Updated".
- The mod's name and authors sit closer together on a card.
- The empty favorite star only shows on hover or focus; favorited mods
  and touch screens always show it. No empty count beside Favorites.
- Links inside sentences are underlined, so themes whose main colour is
  near the text colour (Independents, Lavender) still show them.
- About has a GitHub button with GitHub's mark.
- The AI sparkle beside summaries is a little smaller.
- A mod page labels the thread's own title as "Original title".

title: A mod's shown name is the LLM's where it agrees with the title
body:
The tidying rules cannot take every thread title apart: "Sea of Stars
0.5.1 - Go Beyond the Persean Sector" has a bare version in the middle and
a subtitle behind it, and came through whole. Where the LLM's name for the
mod matches the title by modNamesMatch, that name is shown instead. The
shown name is worked out once per mod, so cards, the release feed and
"Requires" links agree. Ids are unchanged.

title: The site can be shown in any of TriOS's themes
body: Settings has a row of themes to pick from: Default plus eight copied from TriOS, each shown with a strip of its colours. Default still follows the computer's light or dark setting. Each theme's second colour marks whatever is switched on, such as the current page, a ticked choice or a filter in use.

title: Browse can sort mods in a random order
body: Random is a new sort. The order comes from a seed kept in the address, so turning a page or changing a filter keeps the same shuffle and a shared link brings it back. A Shuffle button beside the dropdown draws a new order.

title: Browse can show only mods that are safe to add mid-game
body: A new "Safe to add mid-game" switch keeps only mods whose author says they can go into a game already in progress.

title: A mod's page answers "can I add it mid-game?" and "can I remove it?" in one box
body:
Under the Requires line, a Save compatibility box asks both questions, each with a Yes, No or Depends chip and the author's words in quotes. A question the author never answered shows Unknown. Updating stays beside the version number, which now also shows "it depends" answers, and a mod that can't be removed later gets a badge at the top.

The mod's own file now carries the short answers (canAdd, canUpdate, canRemove) beside the author's words.

title: Home page sections stand out, and categories are called categories
body:
The home page's section headings are bigger and ruled off underneath, and Browse by category has its own See all link. Categories are called categories everywhere a reader sees them.

Also here: the results viewer's labels and messages are shorter and plainer, and a new glossary names the things the catalog collects.

title: Save notes split into adding, updating and removing
body:
A mod's page now shows what the author says about adding the mod to a save, updating it and removing it as separate rows. An updating note only shows for the version it was written for. Releases on the home page carry a "Keeps existing saves" or "Breaks existing saves" badge, and the release feed adds a Saves line.

Also here: Favorites uses Browse's cards and rows and offers undo after Clear all, Browse shows categories as a table, the local site server reloads open pages when a site file changes, and the viewer's code comments are shorter.

title: My list is now Favorites, and the Mod authors page is gone
body:
Press the star on a mod to favorite it. Favorites are shared with Copy URL, and
links shared under the old address still open the page. The Mod authors tab and
its ranking of people by mod count are gone, though a person's own page and
"More by the author" stay, and the search box still suggests people, listed by
name.

title: A mod announced only on Discord shows its download link, not just a button to the post
body:
Every download the site published came off a forum thread, so a mod with no
thread fell back to an "On Discord" button while its download link sat unread in
ModRepo.json. The Discord reader had it all along, as DirectDownload or
DownloadPage on the merged mod. It is now the last fallback, used only when no
thread download exists, so a mod with both is unchanged.

Two rules keep it honest. Not every one of those URLs is a download: the Discord
reader stores a mod's own forum thread as the download page when the
announcement had no link of its own, and those go, along with Discord message
links, subreddit links and anything already one of the mod's own buttons. And
DirectDownload only means the scraper's probe thought the URL was downloadable,
so the host decides whether the button says "Download" or "Download page", and
directUrl is set only where a file really arrives.

The mod page's fallback button now carries its site icon, and the Discord one
is Discord's own filled mark rather than an outline approximation.

title: Removed some text slop. Added favicon slop.
The picture at the top of a mod's page shows whole rather than cropped to the box.
Search doesn't do only first item. Mod images don't crop.
Rename "People" to "Mod authors" across site
Every mod has its own web address
body:
Opening a mod on Starmodder now puts `mods/<id>/` in the address bar. Pasting
that address into Discord shows the mod's name, picture and description. Back
and Forward move between mods and the rest of the site, and nothing reloads on
the way.

title: Browse no longer labels save compatibility
Home now opens with recently added mods
Pages return to where the reader left them
body: Back, Forward, and reload restore one saved position per address. A delayed restoration stops before it can move a newly opened page.

title: Screenshots can be zoomed and swiped
body: The viewer supports wheel, pinch, double-press, keyboard, and drag gestures. It preloads nearby pictures, reports load failures, keeps keyboard focus inside, and offers the original file.

title: Explain how the recent updates list can be wrong
Remember where each page was left
body: Mod pages show AI summaries in their own section. Single-mod threads are no longer labelled as shared threads.

title: Enable header search to select first suggestion with Enter and move support links near main actions
Show each mod's original page beside its download
body: Cards and rows now use a compact source icon for the forum, Discord, or Nexus. Card hover outlines are quieter.

title: About Starmodder in plain English
body: The page answers how the site works, where its data comes from, who made it, and how AI summaries and releases work. Its project and creator names link to their GitHub pages.

title: Search help opens only when you point at the search box.
The empty-results button has room above it.
AI summary tooltips now include the summary itself.
Show the published data behind each mod page
body: A closed raw-info section can copy the mod JSON or open its published file.

title: Explain how recent updates are detected
body: The home page now says that updates come from twice-daily forum checks and AI-read version changes. The full limits and confirmation rules are available in a dialog.

title: Search Starmodder with full matching controls
body: Browse now supports commas, required terms, exclusions, field filters, acronyms, versions, and Best match sorting. Every search box uses the same matching rules and explains what they understand.

title: Choose mod pictures and search suggestions from the keyboard
body: Settings now switches between forum-post pictures and Discord or Nexus announcement pictures. The top-bar search uses the shared match score, explains its syntax, and supports arrow keys and Enter.

title: Publish every grounded forum mod on Starmodder
body: Mods found only in forum threads now get pages, and pages sharing a name link to each other with details that tell them apart. Forum follow-ups can supply downloads, descriptions, and gallery images. Published records also keep announcement pictures and distinguish variants from add-ons.

title: Read every author opening post as one thread
body: Downloads and screenshots in consecutive author follow-ups now reach extraction, bundles, diffs, and the viewer. Collection threads keep each download beside its mod and preserve the author’s description for each entry.

title: Mods that share a forum thread now get their own page
body: A thread holding several mods, like "Hartley's Miscellaneous Mods", now publishes each one with its own page, download, picture and version, and "Part of" the thread under the name. Donation buttons, badges and avatars are never offered to the AI picking a mod's picture; on a single-mod thread it uses the banner at the top. In the results viewer, a live run offers "What this run has changed so far" against the data on disk, a comparison lists only the entries that really moved, and the build line under the status chip works on the deployed copy.

title: Removed "Show Changelogs" text.

How much AI-written summary you see is now three choices rather than on or off, the same three TriOS offers: Always, Only if missing, Never. Always puts the AI paragraph above the author's post on a mod's page rather than instead of it; Only if missing, the default, shows the author's own words and keeps the AI sentence on hover; Never means never, hover included. Anyone who turned the old setting off keeps it off. A mod with a forum thread no longer says "Discord only", since its page offers that thread. "Read changelog" now has its own line under a release, leaving the download button alone at the right. Every tab reads "Nexerelin | Starmodder" instead of using a dash. Browse printed the word "null" where the categories go when nothing matched.

Every list on Starmodder now offers one download button rather than none or four, and it says where pressing it goes: "Install with TriOS", "Download", "Download page", or — for the two hundred and twenty-three mods with nothing to download — "On the forum" or "On Discord", so no card on the site is a dead end. Which download it offers is worked out the same way TriOS's own catalog works it out: a TriOS link first, then anything that hands over the file, then anything that opens somebody's download page, with a plain link ahead of a mirror. My mod list used to draw a button for every download a mod had, four buttons all saying much the same thing, and it fetched each listed mod's whole page to find them; it now costs nothing to draw. The button is the same width all the way down a list, and how many downloads a mod has is a small "2 downloads" among its other facts, because a button that grew to fit its label left the right edge of a page ragged.
body: Settings moved out of the bar at the top into a box of its own, holding how much room there is between things — Dense or Comfortable, the words and pictures the same size either way — and whether AI-written summaries are shown at all. Those summaries now carry a sparkle and a line saying where the words came from, rather than a badge in a different colour. Recent updates has one button that opens every changelog on the page and closes them again, and the mods added recently sit near the top in whole rows, one by default and up to three, with the choice kept between visits. Nexus Mods is no longer read or mentioned anywhere on the site.

title: Starmodder now follows your computer's choice of light or dark pages, in the same cyan-on-navy colours either way. Mod names are plain white and cyan is kept for the things you can actually do, so a page of cards reads as names rather than as forty links. The headings are bigger and to one scale, the boxes are gone from the filters and the panels, and there is more room between everything. Home opens by saying what the site is, then the search box, then the kinds of mod, then what came out recently — the mods added lately have moved to the foot. The parts of a page are named for a screen reader, the number of matching mods is read out as you change the filters, and every piece of writing on the site was checked for readable contrast in both the light and the dark version.

A mod's page now opens with its picture beside the name, the versions and whether it can go in a save you have already started, and the download and the forum thread are the first two buttons — for the three hundred mods with no download link the thread is the download button, so no page is a dead end any more. Screenshots open over the page with the arrow keys instead of as a raw image in a new tab, and the page ends with more by the same people and other mods of the same kind rather than just stopping. You can tick mods into a list of your own, kept in your browser and nowhere else, see it on one page with every download and everything it still needs, and share the whole thing as a single link. Every mod also gets a small page of its own, so pasting a link into Discord shows that mod's name and picture instead of the site's front page, and a search engine sees nine hundred mods rather than one.

Starmodder now files every mod under thirteen categories of its own, mapped from the 26 overlapping names the forum and Discord use between them, and shows them as a row of chips with counts on Home and Browse instead of a dropdown nobody could read. "Discord Only" is no longer a category — it said where a mod was found, not what it is, so a mod's page now says which sites it was found on and its card carries a "Discord only" badge. Mod pages say what a mod will not run without, right above the download and linked to those mods' own pages, and Browse can filter on it; the LLM reads that off the post and any name the post does not actually mention is thrown away. The releases are also written out as a feed anyone can subscribe to, offered from the bar at the top, the foot of every page and the home page. The names each source files a mod under are still shown, in the Details box on its own page.

Starmodder, a public website built from what the scraper already collects, now lives in the repo: a home page led by mods that really did put out a new version, a browse page with search and filters, a page per mod at an address that never changes, a page per person, and an About page saying where all this comes from and how to get a wrong entry fixed. Mod names no longer carry the thread title's brackets, version numbers and leading dashes, and a mod's description is now the author's own forum post with its paragraphs, lists and links kept, rather than whichever line the merge happened to like best. Screenshots are screenshots: donation buttons, build badges, avatars and tiny pictures are left out. Browse opens on mods for the current game release, most recently released first, with the older ones one click away, and "0.98", "0.98a" and "0.98a-RC8" are one choice instead of three. There is a search box in the bar at the top of every page and "/" puts the cursor in it. Fixed a summary that is only a download link being shown as a description, pages keeping the last page's scroll position, and release rows giving no sign they open.
